subject: Enclave access model, CMK custody, and audit evidence
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@mediscribe.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, legal@mediscribe.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Enclave access model, CMK custody, and audit evidence

Hi Kimberly / Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. Mediscribe is evaluating a private deployment (VPC peering) for PHI workloads and we need clarity on three things before procurement:

1) CMK ownership: we require customer-controlled master key (BYOK) and an explicit statement that Redwood will not retain an unencrypted copy of the CMK or the plaintext key material. Please confirm the crypto handoff pattern and whether Redwood ever holds an intermediate wrap key for transient operations.

2) Operator access and observability: our regulators expect zero standing operator access to customer data and a documented breakglass flow. We need a sample operator-access playbook showing the least-privilege role, ephemeral session records, and approval workflow.

3) Audit evidence & retention: samples of attestation logs, KMS usage ledger, and evidence we can present in a third-party audit (SOC2 + healthcare-specific inflows). Also confirmation of log retention windows and whether we can request on-demand exports (signed).

Procurement timeline: legal would like draft contract language and sample evidence by EOD Friday (2026-08-06). Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Elaine
Senior Security Manager
Mediscribe Health
[attachment: requirements_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@mediscribe.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave access model, CMK custody, and audit evidence

Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. We can support the model you describe; below is a high-level summary and next steps.

Summary options (we will provide contract language for both):
- BYOK (recommended): Customer supplies CMK (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / HSM). Redwood performs only wrapped-key usage; we never store unwrapped key material. Customer retains full control for rotate/revoke.
- Customer-keystore-with-escrow: Customer maintains primary CMK but opts to allow Redwood a wrapped escrow key held in HSM for emergency support. Escrow access requires documented, customer-approved breakglass.

Operator access controls we propose:
- Operator role = limited-support-only (no data-plane decryption rights).
- Access windows = explicit ticket + MFA + customer approval; ephemeral session recording pushed to customer S3/Blob.
- Telemetry: we can redact token prefixes and only log operational metrics (latency, errors) unless customer enables full traces for debugging.

Audit evidence we will attach:
- sample_clause_draft.docx (contract appendix language for DPA/Annex)
- kms-attestation-example.pdf (masked example of KMS usage ledger)

Irene and Marissa — can you pull a minimal playbook and the sample attestation artifacts for Friday? We should also prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum for the DPA (legal wants a single-file patch).

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Elaine Park <elaine.park@mediscribe.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave access model, CMK custody, and audit evidence

Elaine / Kimberly — attaching the draft language and an example attestation PDF. Key points we added to the contract appendix:

- No retention of plaintext CMK by Redwood. Clause: "Redwood shall not store, persist, or otherwise retain the plaintext customer master key or any unwrapped form of that key outside of customer-controlled KMS or HSM unless expressly authorized in writing by Customer for a named, time-limited support event."

- Operator breakglass: "Any operator access that would expose data-plane decryption requires an explicit breakglass request, signed by two customer approvers, and is limited to a single session. All sessions shall be recorded and the recording transmitted to Customer's audit bucket within 24 hours."

- Audit evidence: we can provide weekly signed attestations of KMS calls, HSM usage ledgers (redacted to hide other customers), and a signed index for exports. Retention: default 3 years; extended retention (7 years) available as an add-on (we'll mark as procurement option).

I've attached: sample_clause_draft.docx; kms-attestation-example.pdf

[attachment: sample_clause_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
[attachment: kms-attestation-example.pdf (application/pdf)]

I suggest a short tech deep-dive to show the telemetry masking and proof that no plaintext key material is ever exported. Marissa — can you schedule a 45-minute demo?

— Irene Choi
Director, Security Engineering

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@mediscribe.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, legal@mediscribe.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave access model, CMK custody, and audit evidence

Thanks, Irene and Kimberly — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal & procurement:

- Please put the 7-year retention option in the addendum as a checkbox. We may need it for certain legacy clinical records.
- We need a DocuSign-ready DPA addendum (single PDF) we can circulate to our counsel.
- Regulator requires certified, timestamped KMS usage logs for 7 years for selected keys. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide signed exports on demand and an export format (we prefer a signed JSONL with HMAC + timestamp).

Procurement note: target signature week of Aug 17. If you can provide the addendum + example signed export and the operator-playbook by EOD Friday (Aug 6), we can hit that timeline.

Thanks,
Elaine
